units.name: Algebra and Graphs
units.summary: Turning equations into pictures you can read.

topics.name: Straight Line Graphs
topics.summary: Plotting y = mx + c, and what the numbers mean on the picture.

lessons.title: Straight Line Graphs and y = mx + c

objectives.text: Plot a straight line from its equation.
Identify the gradient and y-intercept from an equation.
Read the gradient and intercept off a drawn graph.

keyTerms.definition: How steep the line is: how far up it goes for each step right.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.
A pair (x, y) giving a point’s position.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body: An equation and a graph are the same information in two forms. By the end of this lesson you will be able to move between them in both directions.

sections.heading: Plotting from an equation
sections.body:
Take y = 2x + 1.

Choose some values of x, work out y, and you get points to plot:

    x = 0 →  y = 2(0) + 1 = 1   →  (0, 1)
    x = 1 →  y = 2(1) + 1 = 3   →  (1, 3)
    x = 2 →  y = 2(2) + 1 = 5   →  (2, 5)
    x = 3 →  y = 2(3) + 1 = 7   →  (3, 7)

Plot those four points and they fall in a straight line. Join them and extend.

Three points is enough, and the third is a CHECK: if one point is off the line, you made an arithmetic slip, and you would never notice with only two.

sections.heading: What m and c mean
sections.body:
Every straight line can be written:

    y = mx + c

    m is the GRADIENT — how steep
    c is the Y-INTERCEPT — where it crosses the y-axis

In y = 2x + 1: m = 2 and c = 1. The line crosses the y-axis at 1, and for every 1 step right it climbs 2 up.

The gradient is a rate. m = 2 means "2 up for every 1 across".

    Large m → steep
    Small m → gentle
    NEGATIVE m → the line goes DOWN as you move right

c is easy to find from the equation and easy to read off a graph, so it is usually the first thing to identify.
sections.example:
Reading a line off a graph.

A line crosses the y-axis at 3. From the point (0, 3) it passes through (2, 7).

Find c:
    It crosses the y-axis at 3, so c = 3.

Find m:
    From (0, 3) to (2, 7):
    across:  2 − 0 = 2
    up:      7 − 3 = 4
    gradient = up ÷ across = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

So the equation is y = 2x + 3.

Check with a point you did not use. Try x = 1:
    y = 2(1) + 3 = 5, so (1, 5) should be on the line. It is ✓

Always check with a point you did not use to build the answer. Checking with one you already used proves nothing.

sections.heading: Negative gradients
sections.body:
If m is negative, the line falls as you go right.

    y = −3x + 6

    c = 6, so it crosses the y-axis at 6.
    m = −3, so every 1 step right goes 3 DOWN.

    x = 0 → y = 6
    x = 1 → y = 3
    x = 2 → y = 0

The sign of m tells you the direction; the size tells you the steepness. Reading only the number and ignoring the sign is the most common error here.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.body:
1. Plot y = x + 2 for x = 0, 1, 2, 3.
2. For y = 4x − 5, write down m and c.
3. A line crosses the y-axis at −1 and passes through (3, 5). Find its equation.
4. Without plotting, say which is steeper: y = 2x + 9 or y = 5x − 1. Why?
5. Describe the shape of y = −2x + 4 before plotting it.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
• Choose x values, calculate y, plot the points, join them.
• Use three points so the third checks the other two.
• y = mx + c: m is gradient, c is y-intercept.
• Gradient = up ÷ across, measured between two points.
• Negative m means the line falls to the right.
• Check your equation with a point you did not use.

questions.question: In y = 3x + 4, what is the y-intercept?
questions.explanation: In y = mx + c, c is the y-intercept, so it is 4 — the line crosses the y-axis at 4. The 3 is the gradient, telling you the line climbs 3 for every 1 across. Mixing up m and c is the usual error.

questions.question: A line passes through (0, 3) and (2, 7). What is its gradient?
questions.explanation: Gradient = up ÷ across. Up: 7 − 3 = 4. Across: 2 − 0 = 2. So 4 ÷ 2 = 2. Answering 4 means you found the rise but forgot to divide by the horizontal distance.

questions.question: What does a NEGATIVE gradient tell you about a line?
options: It falls as you move to the right
It is steeper than a positive gradient
It does not cross the y-axis
questions.explanation: A negative gradient means the line goes DOWN as x increases. The sign gives the direction and the size gives the steepness, so y = −5x is steep and falling while y = −0.5x is gentle and falling. A line with negative gradient can still sit above the x-axis.
